summary: The note outlines cybersecurity measures SMEs can adopt to protect digital assets, from understanding threats like phishing and ransomware to risk assessments, employee training, access control, software and hardware, incident response, cloud services, regulatory compliance, and continuous monitoring. It cites various experts, studies and statistics from 2023-2024 and concludes that SME cybersecurity is an ongoing process requiring vigilance and adaptation.
one_line: A guide to the main cybersecurity practices SMEs should adopt, with expert quotes and statistics, to protect digital assets against evolving cyber threats.
key_facts: A Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency study released October 15, 2023 found phishing attacks remain the most common cyber threat for small businesses.
The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) corroborated this, noting a significant surge in phishing activity in the past year.

Emily Sanders said at a November 2, 2023 webinar on cyber resilience that "SMEs are capable of implementing robust cybersecurity measures; it's about prioritizing and understanding the specific threats they face."
The Global Cybersecurity Index released a guide for SMEs on conducting cybersecurity assessments on January 5, 2024.
John Carter, CTO of a fintech startup, said at the "SecureTech for SMEs" summit on February 20, 2024 that a comprehensive assessment pinpointed previously unnoticed data leaks.
A TechSafe survey published March 12, 2024 found human error accounts for approximately 95% of security breaches.
Maria Gonzalez presented findings at the "Data Secure" conference on June 6, 2024 that implementing user privileges reduced insider threat risk by up to 60%.
CyberSafeTech announced a new line of budget-friendly security products for SMEs in a press release dated July 23, 2024.
David Smith, CEO of SecureSME, commented on September 7, 2024 that companies with an established incident response plan recovered 70% faster than those without one.
Cloud services offer SMEs integrated security such as multi-factor authentication (MFA), regular security audits, and compliance with international security standards.
Eleanor Wu's commentary published August 14, 2024 advised choosing a reputable cloud provider with a strong security track record.

Regulations such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) give businesses a framework for data protection and privacy; Robert James's article dated September 23, 2024 says compliance also guides secure infrastructure.
Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems are becoming more accessible and provide an overview of the security status of digital assets.
